blocks.text: 05-SET / store setup and tech Goes here. A high-level overview of customer experience (CX) management principles, emphasizing purpose-driven business, emotional connections, and transitioning from random to intentional customer experiences. Not here. • Paid media campaign setup -> 06-MEA • Landing page optimization for conversions -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides foundational concepts for understanding the importance of customer experience and the methodology behind customer journey mapping. modules: [SET] topics: [customer experience, CX strategy, customer journey mapping, emotional connection, intentional experiences, purpose-driven business] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. defining customer experience / explaining that CX is an expertise and mindset ensuring a great journey for both customers and employees; emotional impact / highlighting that customer experiences are defined by how they make people feel, which directly influences future behavior and commercial benefits; customer-centricity / emphasizing the need to place the customer at the center of the organization, referencing Amazon's practice of keeping an empty "customer chair" in meetings; market shifts / noting the rise of customers, employees, and investors who prioritize companies that "do good" and solve social problems; intentional vs. random experiences / describing the evolutionary phases of CX, moving from inconsistent "random" experiences to designed "intentional" experiences, and finally to "differentiated" experiences; the CX framework / introducing a three-part framework consisting of strategy (defining the desired experience), measurement (using journey mapping to focus improvements), and people (creating a culture that enables employees to act in the customer's interest).
The Amazon "Customer Chair": The anecdote about Amazon leaving an empty chair in every meeting room to represent the customer, ensuring their perspective is considered in all decisions.

Intentional vs. Random Experiences: The concept that organizations must actively design their customer interactions rather than leaving them to chance, a transition that can take years to fully achieve.
Emotion Drives Behavior: The core principle that the way a customer feels during an interaction directly dictates their subsequent actions (e.g., returning, advocating, or leaving).
Skip. The interactive exercises (e.g., drawing a smiley face, drawing the company structure), the promotional mentions of a future workshop, and the Q&A session at the end of the video.
Scope mix. 100% baseline (general customer experience concepts and theories). Volume. ~350 words.
